extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners; patent owners and patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, filing, and examining patent owner and third‑party submissions in ex parte reexamination proceedings, including timing, service, entry/entry‑refusal, extensions, defective papers, and termination consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory action extensions after final rejection (PTOL-467)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an advisory action cannot be mailed in sufficient time for the patent owner to consider the examiner’s position with respect to the amendment after final rejection, the examiner may grant additional time to complete the response. The advisory action form PTOL-467 states: 'THE PERIOD FOR RESPONSE IS EXTENDED TO RUN ___ MONTHS FROM THE MAILING DATE OF THE FINAL REJECTION.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill 'MONTHS' with an integer (2,3,4,5, or 6); fractional months not allowed. In no case can the extension exceed six months from the mailing date of the final rejection. An appropriate response (e.g., second/subsequent amendment or notice of appeal) must be filed within the extended period. If an amendment is filed it must place the reexamination in condition for allowance; otherwise prosecution will stand terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(d) unless an appropriate notice of appeal was filed before expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions to submit affidavits or declarations after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners frequently request extensions after final rejection to submit affidavits/declarations; granting such an extension is without prejudice to the examiner questioning necessity or timing of the affidavit/declaration (37 CFR 1.116(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner’s showing is insufficient the examiner may deny entry of the affidavit despite granting an extension. Granting the extension merely keeps prosecution from terminating while allowing the patent owner to present the affidavit or take other action. Admission or refusal of the affidavit for other purposes does not save prosecution from termination. Affidavits/declarations submitted after final are subject to same treatment as amendments after final (see In re Affidavit Filed After Final Rejection). Prosecution to save must include timely, complete, and proper action as required by 37 CFR 1.113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply requirements to non‑final Office actions (37 CFR 1.111(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to reconsideration or further examination, the reply must be reduced to writing which 'distinctly and specifically points out the supposed errors in the examiner’s action' and must reply to every ground of objection and rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must present arguments pointing out specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references. A general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without specific explanation does not comply. A request may be made to hold form objections in abeyance until allowable subject matter is indicated. The reply must appear to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application or reexamination to final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reply entry conditions (37 CFR 1.111(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply to a reply in compliance with § 1.111(b) will not be entered as a matter of right except as provided; the Office may enter a supplemental reply only if clearly limited to certain topics or filed during suspension under § 1.103(a) or (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted limited subjects: (A) cancellation of claim(s); (B) adoption of examiner suggestion(s); (C) placement of the application in condition for allowance; (D) reply to Office requirement made after first reply; (E) correction of informalities (e.g., typographical errors); (F) simplification of issues for appeal. A supplemental reply filed in sufficient time to be entered before examiner considers prior response may be approved after a cursory review for limitation to these conditions. If not approved for entry, contents should be included in a proper response to a subsequent Office action if the patent owner wishes them considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reply must identify patentable novelty (37 CFR 1.111(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: In amending in reply to a rejection the applicant/patent owner must clearly point out the patentable novelty believed present and show how the amendments avoid cited references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies to applications and reexaminations; show specific claim language distinctions and how amendments overcome prior art or objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of ex parte reexamination proceedings (37 CFR 1.550(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: All ex parte reexamination proceedings, including appeals, will be conducted with special dispatch; after issuance of the order and expiration of response time, examination is conducted in accordance with §§ 1.104–1.116 and will result in an ex parte reexamination certificate under § 1.570.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the reexamination like an expedited examination under those cited sections; follow the same procedural rules unless otherwise specified in 1.550.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response period and normal timing in reexamination (37 CFR 1.550(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding will be given at least thirty days to respond to any Office action. The patent owner will normally be given a period of 2 months to respond; extensions are only under 37 CFR 1.550(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note 37 CFR 1.136 does not apply in reexamination proceedings; where relevant follow the specific reexamination timing rules in 1.550 and MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for requesting extensions of time (37 CFR 1.550(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for an extension must specify the requested period and be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(g). Different filing deadlines and standards apply depending on whether it is a third‑party requested reexamination or a patent‑owner requested/Director‑ordered reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third‑party requested: request must be filed on or before the day action is due; filing alone does not effect extension; will not be granted absent sufficient cause or for more than reasonable time. Patent‑owner requested/Director‑ordered: requests for up to two months must be filed no later than two months from expiration of the time period set; requests for more than two months must be filed on or before the day action is due and will not be granted absent sufficient cause and not for more than reasonable time; no extension beyond statutory maximum. The reply/action must be filed prior to expiration of the extension and never later than the maximum statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file timely and appropriate response — termination and revival (37 CFR 1.550(d),(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response (or required interview statement), prosecution in the ex parte reexamination proceeding will be a terminated prosecution and the Director will issue a certificate concluding the reexamination under § 1.570.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under § 1.137 may be filed to revive a reexamination prosecution terminated under paragraph (d) if the delay was unintentional. Examiner must ensure proper notices/form letters where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party requester participation limits (37 CFR 1.550(g) and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: The active participation of the ex parte reexamination requester ends with the reply pursuant to § 1.535; no further submissions on behalf of the requester will be acknowledged unless in accordance with § 1.510 or § 1.535, or entered prior to the order under § 1.525.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the requester’s active participation ends, any further third‑party submissions must meet requirements of § 1.501(a) and be treated per § 1.501(a) or § 1.535; otherwise they will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements for papers in third‑party requested reexamination (37 CFR 1.550(f), 1.510)
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing a third‑party reexamination request, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third‑party requester must be served on the other party in the manner provided by § 1.248, and the document must reflect service or it may be refused consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach a certificate of service to the paper indicating name/address/method of the party served. A copy of the certificate must be attached to the copy served on the other party. If filed without proof of service the paper may be denied consideration; Central Reexamination Unit should contact submitter to confirm whether service actually occurred and annotate the file accordingly. If no service was made and submitter cannot be contacted, the submission is placed in the reexamination file but normally not considered and marked N/E in the IFW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner must not file third‑party papers (37 CFR 1.550(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner must not file papers on behalf of a third party. If a third‑party paper accompanies, or is submitted as part of, a timely filed patent owner response, the entire submission is considered improper and returned to the patent owner; the third‑party paper will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision returning the improper response and third‑party paper should provide an appropriate extension under 37 CFR 1.550(c), if prior to a final rejection, to refile the response without the third‑party paper. See MPEP § 2254 and § 2267 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) restrictions in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner cannot submit an application data sheet (ADS) in a reexamination proceeding except as provided in MPEP § 2258.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 2258.02 for any allowed ADS submission circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'not fully responsive' to a non‑final Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: A response is not fully responsive where: (A) a bona fide response to a non‑final action is filed; (B) filed before expiration of permissible response period (including extensions); and (C) through apparent oversight or inadvertence some point necessary to a full response has been omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This concept allows entry of corrective practice analogous to 37 CFR 1.135(c) for applications, and only applies where omission is inadvertent and submission is bona fide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner options when submission is not fully responsive (pre‑final)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent owner’s amendment/response prior to final rejection is not fully responsive and meets A–C above, the examiner should not terminate prosecution but may: (A) waive deficiencies (if not serious) and act on the submission; (B) accept the amendment as a response but notify the patent owner via a new Office action setting a new time period for response to supply the omission; or (C) notify the patent owner that the response must be completed within the remaining period for response (or extension) to avoid termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Option (C) should only be used where there is sufficient time remaining. If a minor deficiency exists (e.g., fails to treat every rejection), the examiner may issue a new non‑final or final Office action identifying omitted parts and what is needed. For serious deficiencies or insufficient time, give a new time period to supply omitted matter and warn of termination under 37 CFR 1.550(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 22.14 use for not fully responsive submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 22.14 may be used where a bona fide response is not entirely responsive to a non‑final Office action; it notifies that the communication is not fully responsive and sets a shortened statutory period to supply omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should explain omitted point in bracket 2 and set the time in bracket 3 (ONE MONTH or thirty days, whichever is longer for third‑party requested reexaminations; TWO MONTHS for patent owner requested, Director‑ordered, or 35 U.S.C. 257). Paragraph notes: do not use where omission was deliberate; only for pre‑final responses; after final use PTOL‑467 advisory action instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice limitations for supplying omitted matter (inadvertence and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of giving time to supply an omission applies only when omission was inadvertent and the submission is bona fide, and only prior to final Office action; once inadvertence is brought to patent owner’s attention the question of inadvertence no longer exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply this practice after final Office action — after final, use an advisory Office action (PTOL‑467) to explain omission. If response to notification raises a different inadvertently omitted matter, a second Office action may be given. Examiner should avoid allowing abuse to gain extra time; if no contact attempt succeeds, follow formal notice practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑final amendments entry standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments after final rejection are approved for entry only if they place the proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate or in better form for appeal; otherwise they are not approved for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment after final should be denied entry if some point necessary for a complete response under 37 CFR 1.113 was omitted, even if omission was inadvertent. Where a post‑final submission (e.g., under 1.116) does not place the proceeding in condition for a certificate, the response period continues to run until a response under 1.113 is filed. Examiner may enter response, withdraw final action, and issue a new Office action (Ex parte Quayle) if that course is appropriate, but must be mindful of patent owner rights and inability to refile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective (informal) submissions — common defects and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission may be defective (an 'informal submission') even if its substance is complete. Examples of defects: (A) no proof of service; (B) unsigned paper; (C) signed by non‑practitioner not of record; (D) amendment not complying with 37 CFR 1.530(d)–(j); (E) amendment not complying with 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and/or (4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms PTOL‑475 (for ex parte third‑party requested) and PTO‑2311 (for patent owner requested/Director‑ordered) are used to notify of defects. Check appropriate boxes and fill blanks; if more explanation is needed attach separate sheet. Set a period in the form for correction; extension may be requested under 1.550(c). Failure to correct means submission will not be entered; if this causes failure to file a timely and appropriate response, prosecution may be terminated under 1.550(d). If defective response is filed after final, issue advisory PTOL‑467/PTOL‑467A instead of PTOL‑475/PTO‑2311.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling submissions lacking proof of service
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper requiring proof of service is filed without such proof it may be denied consideration. The Central Reexamination Unit should contact the submitter to confirm whether service was inadvertently omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service is confirmed, request a supplemental paper indicating manner/date of service, enter the submission, and annotate: 'Service confirmed by [name] on [date]'. If no service was made or submitter cannot be contacted, place submission in reexamination file and normally do not consider it; add it to IFW history as unentered with 'N/E' notation and annotate why. If no service, mail Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL‑475) giving one month or thirty days (whichever longer) to complete paper with supplemental certificate of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to serve opposing party
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to serve required copies has consequences: (A) for a patent owner statement or third‑party reply, the submission may be refused consideration; (B) for a patent owner response to an Office action, the response may be refused consideration and prosecution may be terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(d) unless the patent owner has otherwise completely responded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will inform parties of lack of consideration where applicable. Use form paragraph 22.15 to notify and set one month/30 days time to supply proof of service in third‑party requested proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition and expunging of inappropriate or untimely papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed during reexamination that are inappropriate because of some defect will be expunged from the official file by marking them 'closed' and 'non‑public'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returning inappropriate submissions complies with regulations and reduces scanning of improper papers. If an inappropriate paper was scanned before discovery of its nature, it cannot be physically returned; instead it is marked non‑public/closed so it does not appear in the active IFW public record. Certain types require approval of the Director or CRU/TC Director or SPRS for expungement (continued list appears in MPEP § 2267).
